annotations.text:
The ask, restated:

1. Add/edit a note next to each game's status.
2. Other players can read it.
3. Saving bumps lastReported, weighted the same as lastChecked.
4. Caution at >48h idle.
5. Warning at >72h idle.

Suppressed on 100% / Goaled / Done.

One real layout change: .mp-tile-status goes from `display:flex` to a wrapping row with a gap.

It already holds two things — the status pill and the ⚐ claimed flag — and now holds up to four. On a narrow column the note button wraps to a second line rather than squeezing the pill.

Your own note renders open; other players' notes stay collapsed behind the button.

A seven-seat table shows ~28 cards. Expanding every note by default would triple the height of the board and bury the thing players come here for — their own progress.

72h is not a new number. It is PROBLEM_STALE_HOURS, already the point at which the host's report calls a slot stalled.

Reusing it means the red badge is a warning shot the player can act on, not a separate standard they have to learn.

Unstarted slots badge too, on a clock that runs from the room link.

They have no tracker timestamps, so without a fallback they would sit silent forever — the one status where 'you have done nothing' is exactly what needs saying. The link going up is a real event, so it is a legitimate origin, not a guess.

The hover copy changes to match: 'Not started — 78h since the room went up.'
